item.text: {"question_id":"2B.8","answer":"Under López Obrador, military and security resources expanded substantially in response to a genuine organized-crime and public-security threat, but the supplied evidence does not establish transparent, proportionate, or procurement-integrity-based use. Military institutions received 72.2% of security-institution spending from 2019 to 2023; military spending rose 41.9% from 2018, civilian spending fell 50.8%, federal security transfers fell 36%, and National Guard personnel rose 51.9%, with 94% military in practice (BATCH-0016-E007). SIPRI reports Mexican military expenditure of $11.8 billion in 2023 and National Guard allocations rising from 0.7% of military expenditure in 2019 to 11% in 2023, while cautioning that military responses to criminal violence in the region can be more violent than conventional responses (BATCH-0047-E001). WOLA attributes to López Obrador the expansion and intended permanence of military public-security deployment and the effort to place the National Guard under Sedena, while reporting fewer armed confrontations and lower absolute levels of some serious violations but continuing excessive-force cases, weak accountability, insufficient transparency, and inadequate strengthening of civilian institutions (BATCH-0047-E009). Contemporary analysis also describes expanded military control over public functions and a secrecy-oriented posture, although its stronger claims are opinion and interpretation rather than audit or legal findings (BATCH-0047-E011). Thus, the record supports a mixed finding: resources plausibly addressed a real security problem, but their scale, military concentration, and institutional effects indicate questionable proportionality and civilian oversight. The supplied evidence does not demonstrate procurement-specific enrichment, corruption adjudications, or deliberate intimidation of foreign neighbors.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0016-E007","BATCH-0047-E001","BATCH-0047-E009"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0047-E011","BATCH-0051-E013"],"limitations_and_gaps":["No supplied evidence provides procurement contracts, audit findings, corruption adjudications, or a direct finding of network enrichment.","Budget growth and military concentration do not by themselves prove disproportionality; the proportionality judgment remains interpretive and threat-baseline dependent.","The evidence concerns security institutions and administration-level policy; SIPRI does not personally attribute spending decisions to López Obrador, while other sources attribute policy direction but not every expenditure or individual abuse.","No supplied evidence establishes deliberate intimidation of neighboring states.","BATCH-0047-E011 is explicitly an opinion article, and BATCH-0051-E013 is an analytical assessment rather than an official audit. The latter supports increased military influence and mixed policy effects but does not independently establish procurement capture."] ,"corrections_made":["Removed the unsupported characterization of possible patronage or institutional capture.","Reframed spending increases and staffing growth as contextual evidence rather than proof of irresponsible resource use.","Separated documented military concentration, centralization, secrecy, and weak civilian oversight from unproven procurement enrichment.","Qualified ruler attribution by distinguishing administration-level figures from sources that directly attribute policy direction to López Obrador.","Retained the genuine security threat, mixed security outcomes, uncertainty about proportionality, and absence of evidence of foreign intimidation."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["Reopen if procurement records, audit findings, corruption adjudications, legislative oversight materials, or evidence concerning military-linked commercial networks become available.","Reopen if source-supported evidence clarifies whether the expanded resources produced proportionate security gains relative to the organized-crime threat.","Reopen if evidence shows cross-border coercion or intimidation connected to the military-resource decisions."]}
